title: Casting a SPELL: Sentence Pairing Exploration for LLM Limitation-breaking
author_or_org: Yifan Huang, Xiaojun Jia, Wenbo Guo
gate_reason: brief_exclusion:code_jailbreak_out_of_scope — SPELL is a comprehensive testing framework specifically designed to evaluate weakness of security alignment in malicious code generation. Brief explicitly rejects 'papers on unrelated jailbreak categories (e.g., image generation, code jailbreaks)'.

title: PIG: Privacy Jailbreak Attack on LLMs via Gradient-based Iterative In-Context Optimization
author_or_org: Yidan Wang, Yanan Cao, Yubing Ren
gate_reason: adjacent_not_material — PIG targets PII extraction via gradient-based ICL, a security/privacy attack with no policy/social science framing. Brief rejects 'technical papers without policy/social science relevance'. The 'knowledge-gated extraction' framing in the why_relevant line is post-hoc.

title: Open Sesame! Universal Black-Box Jailbreaking of Large Language Models
author_or_org: Raz Lapid, Ron Langberg, Moshe Sipper
gate_reason: adjacent_not_material — Genetic-algorithm universal single-turn adversarial prompt. Does not engage with conversational/multi-turn LLM behavior; brief V2 specifically rejects 'papers that don't engage with conversational/multi-turn LLM behavior'. The 'single-turn baseline' rationale in why_relevant is weak — single-turn baselines are amply covered by c068 PAIR and c071 MASTERKEY.

title: From Domains to Instances: Dual-Granularity Data Synthesis for LLM Unlearning
author_or_org: Xiaoyu Xu, Minxin Du, Zitong Li
gate_reason: adjacent_not_material — BiForget is a technical machine-unlearning data-synthesis framework benchmarked on Harry Potter domain. While unlearning is conceptually adjacent to pilot's 'knows but won't say' finding, the paper itself has no engagement with knowledge-gated access, identity, geopolitics, or differential treatment. Brief rejects 'technical papers without policy/social science relevance'.

title: JMedEthicBench: A Multi-Turn Conversational Benchmark for Evaluating Medical Safety in Japanese Large Language Models
author_or_org: Junyu Liu, Zirui Li, Qian Niu
gate_reason: brief_exclusion:medical_domain_specific_not_political — JMedEthicBench evaluates multi-turn medical-safety on Japanese LLMs using Japan Medical Association guidelines. Although methodologically multi-turn, the domain (clinical consultation safety) and content (medical ethics) sit outside the brief's political/identity/geopolitical scope. Brief rejects 'papers about general NLP bias unrelated to political/identity content'.
